paper_metadata.title: Resection Surgery for Partial Epilepsy. Relation of Surgical Outcome with Some Aspects of the Epileptogenic Process and Surgical Approach

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the sample's clinical characteristics and the recruitment setting. However, it is a retrospective series from a single neurosurgical institute, and there is no information regarding the total number of eligible patients versus those included, which introduces potential selection bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: One hundred and thirty-eight epileptic patients submitted to resective surgical treatment in our Institute were considered. Their age ranged from 7 months to 46 years (mean 21.6 years); 100 were males and 38 were females.
items.reasoning: The authors provide age, sex, and basic clinical history of the cohort.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: One hundred and thirty-eight epileptic patients submitted to resective surgical treatment in our Institute were considered.
items.reasoning: While the site is identified, the specific recruitment process (consecutive vs. convenience) and the flow of patients from the total pool of epilepsy patients at the institute are not detailed.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: The duration of epilepsy was of at least three years standing... Malignant tumours and AVMs were excluded. Surgery was performed in all patients according to epileptological criteria... Lesionectomy alone and callosotomy were not considered.
items.reasoning: The authors specify clinical requirements for inclusion and list specific exclusions (malignancy, AVMs, specific surgical types).

items.label: Baseline characteristics

items.evidence_snippet: Seizure type included: complex partial (n = 98), simple partial (n = 37) and secondarily generalized seizures (n = 75). The presence of a causative cerebral structural lesion was documented in 103 cases.
items.reasoning: Key clinical and diagnostic characteristics are tabulated and described.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study reports on a fixed cohort of 138 patients with a minimum follow-up of three years. While it doesn't explicitly detail dropouts, the analysis is presented as a complete set of the treated patients meeting the follow-up criteria.

items.reasoning: The analysis includes all 138 patients who met the inclusion criteria, implying 100% data availability for the defined cohort.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (EEG patterns and surgical extent) are clearly defined and measured using standardized clinical protocols (10-20 system, Stereo-EEG, MRI/CT). The use of a collegial analysis for EEG interpretation reduces individual measurement bias.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Three main spatial patterns were recognized: a) "monofocal": at least 80% of interictal epileptiform abnormalities confined to a given cerebral region...
items.reasoning: The authors provide quantitative thresholds (80%) for defining the spatial patterns of the prognostic factors.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: All the etectrophysiological material... was at first screened by one observer (G.C.), and subsequently submitted to a collegial analysis, involving at least three peopIe.
items.reasoning: The use of a consensus-based (collegial) approach for EEG interpretation enhances reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Three main spatial patterns were recognized: a) "monofocal": at least 80% of interictal epileptiform abnormalities...
items.reasoning: The 80% cut-point is a standard clinical threshold in epilepsy surgery literature.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Invasive EEG studies: they were i) acute (electrocorticography 7z cases, stereo-EEG 4 cases), and/or it) chronic (subdural grids 5 cases, stereo-EEG 43 cases)
items.reasoning: While the diagnostic work-up followed a general protocol, the specific type of EEG (acute vs. chronic, scalp vs. invasive) varied between patients based on clinical need.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: The spatial arrangement of the interictal and of the ictal activities were congruent in 66 cases (67.3%).
items.reasoning: The study reports data for the majority of the cohort, though ictal data was missing for 40 patients.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: It became of paramount importance in the 40 patients lacking sufficient documentation on the electrocerebral ictal activity.
items.reasoning: The authors did not use imputation; they analyzed the subset with available data or shifted the weight of evidence to interictal data.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure freedom) is clearly defined and measured at regular intervals over a 3-year period. The criteria for 'Class I' are stringent (including aura), which reduces the risk of overestimating surgical success.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Class I: complete disappearance of seizures, including aura. We decided not to include in this class the patients who still had auras...
items.reasoning: The outcome classes are explicitly defined with a clear rationale for excluding auras from the success group.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The seizure occurrence as well as the psycho-social adjustment was checked at intervals of six months to one year.
items.reasoning: Regular clinical follow-up is a standard and reliable method for assessing seizure frequency.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The evaluation of the surgical result was related to the first three post-surgical years... checked at intervals of six months to one year.
items.reasoning: A uniform follow-up schedule and duration were applied to the entire cohort.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses multivariable logistic regression to account for confounding between the primary prognostic factors. However, other potential confounders like age of onset, duration of epilepsy, and specific medication changes were not included in the multivariable model.

items.evidence_snippet: Age, sex... duration of the disease; frequency and clinical pattern of the seizures... Full pharmacological medication was maintained for the first two post-surgical years.
items.reasoning: While several clinical variables were measured, they were not all included in the final statistical adjustment.
